reasoning: Both sets are strong single-package plans with spine-first M1s, frozen interfaces and fixture-backed fakes. A wins on content. Its RL design is more teachable and better checked: a ladder from table to DQN to CNN with ablations, REINFORCE against PPO, and a fixed-opponent → naive co-learning → pool self-play ladder. Truncation is kept separate from termination. The golden cases are precise closed forms: Q-update 0.1/0.009, GAE [1.3775, 0.5], clipped objective, and exact tank and predator-prey geometry. These directly support the user's goal of being able to explain why each agent works. A's weaknesses are size and some stale framing. Each stage is one very large milestone, so M1 has 31 tasks and bundles three agents, the corridor, the reference, ablations, the report and replay. CORE-06 still talks about a 'revision' even though AD-09 and AD-13 now adopt the batch-first, team-aware core before M1. Wiring packets carry fish and predator-prey material that M1 does not need. A also freezes private maths helpers in the contract. B splits the stages into seven milestones along mostly real dependency lines (one fish → many → local sight). It adds a useful check-world gate and write-ups. However, B's first milestone has no replay, so the snake cannot be watched until M2. M3 ('Check and explain') is a leftover milestone. M1 claims TRAIN-07, which cannot be tested until the two-team world arrives in M7. B's golden cases are mostly property checks over random rollouts, and several oracles are still open (TC-07 direction and expected score, the TC-17 bound). Some spine packets leave out types they need. B is a little easier to read, but A's specification, tests and build packets are more complete and more accurate, so A edges ahead overall.

strengths: Precise, hand-checkable golden cases (TC-07 compact view, TC-12 Q-update, TC-42 GAE, TC-43 clip, TC-52/TC-58 catch geometry)
Ladders that each teach one RL idea, plus ablations and a reference with a one-to-one hyperparameter mapping (AD-04, AD-10, AD-11)
Truncation and termination kept separate so learning targets bootstrap correctly
Dependency graph uses call and data edges mitigated by fakes; 'none' reasons are mostly valid (e.g. T27→T26 share agent.py)
Context packets carry the frozen types and test cases the task needs
weaknesses: One milestone per stage; M1 alone is 31 tasks covering three agents, the corridor, the reference, ablations, report and replay
Stale 'revision' framing (CORE-06, S2 outline) now that AD-09 and AD-13 are adopted before M1
Private helpers frozen in the contract (agents.returns_to_go, gae, clipped_objective)
Wiring packets include FishTank, PredatorPrey and PPOAgent, which M1 does not need
Dense, hard reading for a learner

strengths: Finer milestones that follow real dependency lines in S2 (one fish → many → local sight)
Check-world gate (TRAIN-06) with a hand-derived two-exit corridor, a good guard against silent RL bugs
A single episode loop (core.play_episode) reused by training, evaluation, replay and the reference check
Fully specified paired permutation test with Holm correction; learner write-ups backed by a finish check
Plainer spec language for a solo learner
